question: If a line judge clearly gets an in/out call wrong, what can the umpire do?

answer.reasoning: The question has one part: what the umpire can/must do when a line judge clearly makes a wrong in/out call. laws-17.5.1 and itto-2.4.1 state the umpire shall overrule the line judge when beyond reasonable doubt the call was clearly wrong; itto-8.2 confirms the overrule supersedes the original line call; itto-5.8.2 with itto-5.8.2.1 and itto-5.8.2.2 give the exact calls the umpire shall immediately make ('Correction, IN' / 'Correction, OUT'). The umpire shall then immediately call "Correction, IN" if the shuttle landed "in", or "Correction, OUT" if the shuttle landed "out" (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26, Clauses 5.8.2, 5.8.2.1 and 5.8.2.2). Any overrule by the umpire supersedes the original line call by the line judge (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 8.2).
